conventions.convention: The tree is finite and directed away from its root; receivers are all nonroot leaves; every nonroot internal vertex has at least two children. The root may have any finite number of children.
Link-success parameters belong to the open cube (0,1)^E, remain fixed across designs and probes, and generate independent repeated observations. Every design has a positive probe count.
Splitting a vertex requires two receivers in distinct child subtrees within one design; the condition applies only to nonroot internal vertices. Coverage includes every receiver.

EM initializes in the open cube but evaluates subsequent candidates in the closed cube using explicitly defined Bernoulli masses. Positive-count patterns must be feasible and every edge must have positive probe exposure. Stopping statuses assert neither convergence nor global optimality.
The Gaussian example assumes AC for the library normal-law convention, uses independent link delays with variance one, and compares joint receiver laws rather than only marginal means.

load_bearing.statement: For link-success parameters p ∈ (0,1)^E, receiver indicators are products of independent Bernoulli link successes along root paths. The complete experiment observes N_d independent outcomes with law P_{p,d} for each design, independently across designs.
The design satisfies the split/coverage condition if every receiver is covered and every nonroot internal vertex is split by at least one design.
For the stated finite-tree multicast loss experiment, the full repeated-probe sampling-law map is injective if and only if the design satisfies the split/coverage condition.
